deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding 1983 'Théories homotopiques' notes, a precursor of Les Dérivateurs): a 'homotopy theory' is presented by a pair (M,W), a category M with a class W of weak equivalences. It gives the system A ↦ H_W(A) = Hom(A,M)[W_A^{-1}], where A runs over small categories and W_A is the class of pointwise (objectwise) weak equivalences. A functor f: M → M' compatible with W, W' induces comparison functors H_W(A) → H_{W'}(A). The page opens with the end of a remark: if these comparisons are equivalences 'for all A', the comparison is fine ('on sera OK').

Criterion. Grothendieck then gives a sufficient condition. Suppose f has a right adjoint g with two properties:
- (i) f^{-1}(W') = W, i.e. f preserves and reflects weak equivalences.
- (ii) the counit fg(X') → X' lies in W' for every X' in M'.

Then postcomposition gives adjoint functors f_*^M: Hom(A,M) ⇄ Hom(A,M'): g_*^M. These satisfy the same two conditions for W_A and W'_A, because everything is pointwise. So the conclusion 'hence H_W(A) ⇄ H_{W'}(A) are quasi-inverse equivalences' holds uniformly in A. He started writing that conclusion and then crossed it out.

Why the criterion works (assuming 2-out-of-3 for W'):
- g preserves W. If u: X'→Y' is in W', naturality of the counit plus 2-out-of-3 puts fg(u) in W'. By (i), g(u) is then in W.
- The unit is in W. The triangle identity gives counit_{fX} ∘ f(unit_X) = id. Since the counit is in W', f(unit_X) is in W', so by (i) unit_X is in W.
- Hence f and g are homotopical, and both unit and counit are weak equivalences. Therefore they induce inverse equivalences of the localizations, and the same holds for every diagram category A.

Definition. Finally he names homotopy theories H that can be described by a single (M,W) 'spéciales'. He remarks that this imposes 'draconian' conditions on (M,W). Presumably these are the conditions needed for A ↦ Hom(A,M)[W_A^{-1}] to have the required functoriality, in particular the Kan-extension and derived-functor properties of a derivator.
errors: Implicit hypothesis: the argument that g preserves weak equivalences, and that the unit is a weak equivalence, needs W' to satisfy 2-out-of-3 (or saturation). This is not stated on the page, though it is presumably a standing assumption.
The conclusion (equivalence of H_W(A) and H_{W'}(A)) was crossed out and is not written down. It is nevertheless correct under the 2-out-of-3 assumption.

ideas.what: Criterion for an adjunction to induce an equivalence of homotopy categories: the left adjoint creates (preserves and reflects) weak equivalences and the counit is a weak equivalence.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopical adjunction / homotopical equivalence; model-free analogue of the Quillen-equivalence criterion (F reflects weak equivalences and the derived counit is a weak equivalence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (1967) for the model-category form; Dwyer–Hirschhorn–Kan–Smith (homotopical categories, 2004); Hovey, Model Categories (1999), Cor. 1.3.16
ideas.where_published: Similar comparison arguments appear in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Passing the criterion to diagram categories via pointwise weak equivalences, so the comparison is an equivalence for all A, i.e. an equivalence of the associated prederivators.
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of (pre)derivators induced by a homotopical equivalence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs); Heller (homotopy theories); Cisinski, Maltsiniotis

ideas.what: Terminology 'théories homotopiques spéciales' for homotopy theories presentable by a single category with weak equivalences, with the remark that this imposes draconian conditions on (M,W).
ideas.modern_name: Representable / presentable derivators (derivators of the form D_{(M,W)})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; later Cisinski and Maltsiniotis on derivators associated to categories with weak equivalences
ideas.where_published: Possibly a precursor of terminology in Les Dérivateurs; the word 'spéciale' in this sense is unsure

missed.claim: This is an early (1983) explicit formulation of the model-free criterion for comparing presentations of homotopy theories at the level of all diagram categories. It is a datable step toward the derivator formalism, seven years before Les Dérivateurs. Mathematically the criterion is standard.
missed.quote: Les théories H qui peuvent se décrire par un (M, W) seront dites spéciales. Cela implique des conditions draconiennes sur (M, W)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents the genesis of derivator ideas and the 'spéciale' terminology. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but standard criterion (homotopical adjunction / Quillen-equivalence analogue) plus an early naming of presentable homotopy theories. Of historical interest for dating derivator ideas, not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: The first line 'pour ∀A, ∃ ? on sera OK' is the end of a sentence from a previous page; the '∃' (superscript 7-like mark) is likely an insertion mark or existential sign, uncertain.
In the Hom diagram the arrows are labelled f^M_* (top) and g^M_* (bottom); an initial 'M' superscript was overwritten.
The crossed-out line reads approximately 'H_W(A) ⇄ H_{W'}(A)' with arrows labelled f^A_W and g^A_W, followed by a heavily struck phrase, perhaps 'Maximum effectuer…'; illegible.
